verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Both halves are present, but in separate declarations rather than one display. First half: `ProblemStatement.navierStokesResidual` is the paper's ℛ(u,p) term for term — ∂_t u (`temporalDerivative`, the ordinary time derivative), (u·∇)u (`advection`, the spatial Fréchet derivative applied to u), −Δu (`spatialLaplacian`, the componentwise Euclidean Laplacian, so the sign and the derivative count agree) and +∇p (`pressureGradient`), at viscosity exactly one as the paper's display also takes it. It is the same operator the local construction uses: `CylindricalResidual.navierStokesResidual_cylindrical` (NavierStokes/CylindricalResidual.lean:495) rewrites it in the cylindrical frame. Second half: no declaration introduces a named object ℛ_*. The exponent 2A+1/2 appears exactly, in two places. `CorrectionStep.RepresentsPhysical` imposes normalized = Q^(2A+1/2) × physical on the residual-class error fields (with Q^A on velocity and Q^(2A) on pressure, matching the p. 101 sentence about the recovery factors Q^(-A), Q^(-2A), Q^(-2A-1/2)); and the hypotheses of `LocalSignedRequest.normalizedRequest_represents` state the same relation for the θ- and z-components of the mean residual, with the chart substitution r ↦ Q^(-1/2) r. `SignedStressPrimitive.normalizedResidual` packages the same normalization as a definition, but with the local slow scale q in place of the band scale Q (and the chart pullback r = √q·R folded in via `nativeSource`); recovering the display from it needs the paper's q ≍ Q, whereas recovering it from `RepresentsPhysical` is a direct read-off. The rewriting is therefore: ℛ(u,p) is `navierStokesResidual` verbatim, and ℛ_* is that field multiplied by `Q n ^ (2 * A + 1 / 2)` as `RepresentsPhysical.baseError` writes it, componentwise in the chart frame.
